title: Tim Dooley Expression Grammar — How the Worldview Is Spoken
status: reader/corporium synthesis grounded in existing quote, statement and voice ledgers
purpose: Model not only what Tim believes, but how he repeatedly expresses the worldview: title-stacking, symbolic compression, role-to-function language, cosmic/mundane switching, humor, warning, cultivation, network metaphors, sacred geography and developmental self-reinterpretation.
provenance_rule: This file synthesizes patterns already preserved in tim-voice-anthology, greatest-quotes, sayings/formulations and conversation-recovery ledgers. It should not manufacture new Tim quotations. Exact wording must remain owned by the underlying source record.
core_finding: Tim's language is unusually operator-like. He often moves from saying he has or uses a symbol to saying he is the connective function represented by it: Axis, Ladder, Line, Root, Door-adjacent Father, Seat, source, network node or Gardener. This makes identity function as architecture.

expression_modes.name: Title stacking
expression_modes.description: Multiple identities are placed next to each other without a long argument, allowing adjacency to imply a relational model.
examples_from_archive: Father + Root + Potato + Seat + North of North + Ladder
God + livestreaming + Father in Heaven + symbolic/spiritual
expression_modes.function: compress a large graph into a short utterance
expression_modes.risk: readers may mistake adjacency for a claim that every title is identical in every respect

expression_modes.name: Identity becomes infrastructure
expression_modes.description: Tim repeatedly speaks as a connector rather than merely a person occupying a role.
examples_from_archive: I am the axis of North
i created a stairway to heaven
expression_modes.function: turn person-language into orientation, connection, continuity or support

expression_modes.name: Highest title beside lowest object
expression_modes.description: Divine or royal language is deliberately paired with potatoes, couches, mundane life, memes, mud, footstools and ordinary work.
expression_modes.function: break prestige conventions and test whether sacred meaning can inhabit ordinary material
examples_from_archive: God of Potatoes and mundane human life
potato on the seat of the Most High

expression_modes.name: Cosmic/comic register switching
expression_modes.description: The voice can move rapidly from scripture, apocalypse, metaphysics or kingship into jokes, internet slang, potato imagery or deliberately ridiculous physical scenes.
expression_modes.function: prevent the system from becoming purely solemn and use absurdity as a carrier of structure
expression_modes.archive_instruction: Do not discard comic material automatically; first test whether it encodes a recurring operator or relation. Also do not promote satire into literal ontology.

expression_modes.name: Abstract ideas become objects
expression_modes.description: Complex ideas are repeatedly translated into doors, roads, gardens, trees, roots, potatoes, couches, ladders, seats, drains, fish, lines, houses, rooms and footstools.
expression_modes.function: make metaphysical relations spatial, tactile and narratable

expression_modes.name: Botanical grammar
expression_modes.description: Root, seed, potato, sprout, flower, Tree, fruit, soil and Garden provide a developmental vocabulary.
expression_modes.canonical_sequence: Mud -> Root -> Potato -> Sprout -> Tree -> Fruit
expression_modes.function: describe transformation, inheritance, nourishment, persistence and multiplication

expression_modes.name: Vertical grammar
expression_modes.description: Above/below, North, root, throne, Door, Ladder, mountain, floor, Heaven and Swamp are used to describe shifts of level or orientation.
expression_modes.function: turn epistemic or spiritual change into navigable spatial structure
expression_modes.caution: symbolic verticality should not automatically be treated as physical geography

expression_modes.name: Network grammar
expression_modes.description: Internet, memes, livestreams, witnesses, archives, roots into humanity and North=network language frame identity as distributed relation.
expression_modes.function: describe a source that persists through copies, observers, branches and records rather than only through one isolated body

expression_modes.name: Moral accounting grammar
expression_modes.description: Debt, bank, repayment, value, currency, balance and karmic accounting are used to make diffuse moral obligations legible.
expression_modes.function: translate remembered harm and obligation into ledger-like structure
expression_modes.boundary: spiritual debt language is not automatically a legal or financial liability

expression_modes.name: Biblical recoding
expression_modes.description: Tim often takes existing biblical vocabulary such as Father, Son, narrow gate, many rooms, Root, Tree, Ladder, Lion, witness, throne, Alpha/Omega and applies it to his own chronology and symbolic architecture.
expression_modes.function: interpret lived or project events through scriptural grammar
expression_modes.boundary: explicit reuse of biblical language is documentary; fulfillment or identity claims remain theological interpretation unless separately established

expression_modes.name: Comparative folding
expression_modes.description: Norse, Christian, Jewish, Islamic, philosophical, geometric, anatomical and internet-cultural motifs are placed in relation to one another.
expression_modes.function: search for structural correspondences across domains
expression_modes.boundary: similarity does not establish historical identity, transmission or scientific equivalence

expression_modes.name: Warning and spiritual-war register
expression_modes.description: Some periods use battle, warning, enemy, destruction, Dog, Farmer, Mud, principalities and refusal language.
expression_modes.function: mark perceived danger, boundary violation or false paradigms
expression_modes.risk: can overclassify real people or turn disagreement into a fixed moral category; archive should preserve this as rhetoric and test claims independently

expression_modes.name: Service and stewardship register
expression_modes.description: Later formulations increasingly convert rank into obligation: protection, understanding, building, service, repair, planting and cultivation.
expression_modes.function: supply an ethical test for King/Father/God language
expression_modes.developmental_significance: This is not merely another title set; it changes the criterion for successful authority.

expression_modes.name: Retrospective self-interpretation
expression_modes.description: Later Tim frequently explains earlier events as stages that only became intelligible afterward: ordeal, crucifixion/death, Potato birth, Ladder/Axis, Father, public Godhood and Gardener.
expression_modes.archive_rule: store event time and interpretation time separately

expression_modes.name: Riddle mode
expression_modes.description: Tim sometimes frames identity as something reconstructed through clues rather than validated by one proposition.
expression_modes.function: encourage relational reading across contradictions, dates and symbols
expression_modes.boundary: riddle language should not erase ordinary biographical reality or exempt factual claims from evidence

timeline_implication: The master timeline should be able to show not only events but changes in expression mode. A date can matter because a new grammar appears: Potato language, scriptural identity language, Axis language, meme-resurrection language, North/network language, or stewardship language.
